inventory.observation: One shared Cartesian-style frame; vertical axis labelled p with upward arrow, horizontal axis labelled V with rightward arrow, and origin mark O. No grid, ticks, numerical scale, units, point names or separate subfigures.

A single thick continuous descending convex curve in the positive quadrant, steep at its upper-left end and flatter at its lower-right end. The upper endpoint is right of the pressure axis and above the upper guide; the lower endpoint is right of both volume-interval guide pairs. The image alone does not establish an exact numerical function.

Four solid horizontal guides from just left of the pressure axis to the curve, with four solid vertical projections down to the volume axis. Upper pair near source pixels (244,228) and (297,367); lower pair near (485,578) and (538,606). These source guide intersections meet the curve. The pairs occupy the same frame, not separate charts.

Two horizontal intervals labelled Delta V, near y=769, between vertical projections at approximately x=244..297 and x=485..538. They appear equally wide. For each, the left short arrow points right toward the left boundary and the right short arrow points left toward the right boundary; the label occupies the intervening space. The arrow shafts and heads are outside the narrow measured interval, not motion arrows along the curve.

A tall vertical dimension left of the pressure axis, between guides near y=228 and y=367, labelled Delta p with subscript 2. Its end heads face the upper and lower guide boundaries; the visible span is much taller than the lower pressure dimension.

A short vertical dimension left of the pressure axis between guides near y=578 and y=606, labelled Delta p with subscript 1. A short upper arrow descends toward the upper boundary and a short lower arrow ascends toward the lower boundary, from outside the narrow span. Label is offset below/left. These are inward external dimension arrows.

Below the volume axis, horizontal dimensions start at the pressure-axis baseline: V2 reaches the second small-volume vertical projection (near x=297) and V1 reaches the second large-volume projection (near x=538). Both have endpoint-directed heads. V1 is visibly longer than V2. The corresponding projection lines extend below the axis to those dimension levels.

An unlabelled isolated thin oblique/curved mark appears above the flatter part of the main curve, approximately x=430..567 and y=461..558. It does not visibly connect to the main curve, axes or dimensions. No physical identity, tangent, path, second isotherm, arrow or mathematical significance is assigned.
